questions.question: Define load, effort and pivot, and identify each one when a worker lifts a boulder with a steel bar resting on a stone.
questions.expected_answer: The pivot or fulcrum is the fixed point the lever turns about: the stone under the bar. The load is the force the lever must overcome, usually the weight of the object being moved: the boulder pressing on the short end. The effort is the force applied by the user: the worker's hands pushing down on the long end of the bar.

questions.question: A load of 800 newtons is lifted with an effort of 100 newtons. Calculate the mechanical advantage and explain in words why the lever gives this advantage.
questions.expected_answer: Mechanical advantage is load divided by effort, so 800 divided by 100 gives 8; the lever multiplies the effort eight times. It gives the advantage because the effort is applied much further from the pivot than the load is: the effort arm is far longer than the load arm, and the longer the effort arm compared with the load arm, the more the force is multiplied.

questions.question: Explain the trade-off involved in using a lever, and describe what happens to the effort and to the distance the load rises if the pivot is moved closer to the load.
questions.expected_answer: A lever that multiplies force makes the effort move a greater distance than the load; force is traded for distance and the lever never gives out more energy than is put in. Moving the pivot closer to the load shortens the load arm and lengthens the effort arm, so the effort needed decreases and the mechanical advantage increases, but the load rises a smaller distance for each push.
